title: AURAWEAR — AI-Powered Fashion Intelligence Platform (MVP)

requirements.text: Build the backend data model and API for the product catalog. Store clothing items with fields: id, name, category, price (INR), description, sizes, colors, tags, imageUrl, stock, and isTrending flag. Expose query functions: getAllProducts, getProductById, getProductsByCategory, and a keyword/tag-based search function (searchProducts) that accepts a natural language query string and returns matching products by matching against name, tags, category, and price range parsed from the query.

quotes: I want casual black oversized hoodie under ₹2000

acceptanceCriteria: Products can be stored and retrieved from the canister.
searchProducts('casual black oversized hoodie under 2000') returns relevant products filtered by tags/price.
getAllProducts returns the full catalog.
isTrending flag can be set and queried.

requirements.text: Build backend support for user Style Profiles. Each profile stores: userId (principal), bodyMeasurements (height, weight, chest, waist, hips), stylePreferences (array: streetwear, minimal, luxury, casual, formal), savedOutfits (array of outfit objects with product IDs), and trendAlerts (array of strings). Expose functions: createOrUpdateStyleProfile, getStyleProfile, saveOutfit, removeSavedOutfit.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can create and update their style profile.
Saved outfits are persisted per user.
Style preferences are stored as an array of enum values.
getStyleProfile returns the full profile for a given principal.

requirements.text: Build backend support for Wardrobe Optimizer. Store a user's wardrobe items (productId or custom item name, category, color). Expose functions: addWardrobeItem, removeWardrobeItem, getWardrobe, and getWardrobeSuggestions which returns a list of product recommendations based on gaps in the user's wardrobe categories and colors.
acceptanceCriteria: Wardrobe items can be added and removed per user.
getWardrobeSuggestions returns products in categories underrepresented in the user's wardrobe.
Outfit combination logic returns at least 5 outfit groupings from wardrobe items.

requirements.text: Build backend support for Trend Radar. Maintain a curated list of trending items (populated by admin or seeded data) with fields: productId, trendScore, trendTags (e.g. 'streetwear 2025', 'earth tones'), and dateAdded. Expose: getTrendingItems, and getPersonalizedTrends(userId) which filters trending items by the user's style preferences.

quotes: Recommends trending pieces personalized to the user

acceptanceCriteria: getTrendingItems returns all items with isTrending=true sorted by trendScore.
getPersonalizedTrends filters trending items to match the user's style preferences.
Trend data is queryable from the frontend.

requirements.text: Build a homepage with: (1) a full-viewport hero section with headline 'Meet Your AI Stylist', tagline 'Your Style. Your Data. Your AI.', and a CTA button 'Start Your Style Journey'; (2) an interactive demo preview section showing a simulated AI outfit recommendation with a sample query input and 3 product card results; (3) a features section showcasing the five AI agents (Style Twin, Occasion Agent, Wardrobe Optimizer, Trend Radar, Virtual Try-On) with icons and brief descriptions; (4) a social proof section with 3 mock testimonials and brand stats (e.g. '10,000+ Styles Generated', '98% Fit Accuracy').
acceptanceCriteria: Hero section is full-viewport with headline, tagline, and CTA visible on load.
Interactive demo section accepts a text query and displays 3 sample product cards.
All five AI agents are described in the features section.
Social proof section displays testimonials and brand stats.

requirements.text: Build an AI Studio page (user dashboard) with four tabs: (1) Style Twin — form to enter body measurements and select style preferences (streetwear, minimal, luxury, casual, formal), save profile to backend, display current profile; (2) Saved Outfits — grid of outfits saved by the user, each showing product thumbnails and a remove button; (3) AI Suggestions — display personalized product recommendations based on the user's style preferences fetched from the backend; (4) Trend Alerts — display trending items personalized to the user's style profile.
acceptanceCriteria: All four tabs are navigable and render correct content.
Style Twin tab saves profile to backend and shows confirmation.
Saved Outfits tab reads from backend and allows removal.
AI Suggestions and Trend Alerts tabs fetch and display data from backend.
Page is accessible without authentication (data scoped to anonymous principal if no login).

requirements.text: Build a Shop page with an 'Ask AI' search bar at the top. When the user types a natural language query (e.g. 'casual black oversized hoodie under ₹2000') and submits, call the backend searchProducts function and display matching products in a responsive grid of product cards. Each card shows: image, name, price in INR (₹), category, available sizes, and an 'Add to Cart' button. Include a category filter sidebar (All, Tops, Bottoms, Outerwear, Accessories, Footwear).

quotes: User types: 'I want casual black oversized hoodie under ₹2000'

acceptanceCriteria: Ask AI search bar is prominently placed at the top of the Shop page.
Submitting a query calls searchProducts and displays results.
Product cards show image, name, INR price, sizes, and Add to Cart.
Category sidebar filters products client-side.
Empty state is shown when no results match.

requirements.text: Build a Wardrobe Optimizer page where users can: (1) add wardrobe items by selecting category and color; (2) view their current wardrobe as a visual grid; (3) click 'Optimize My Wardrobe' to call getWardrobeSuggestions and display recommended products as cards; (4) see suggested outfit combinations (groupings of 3–4 items) generated from their wardrobe.
acceptanceCriteria: User can add and view wardrobe items.
Optimize button triggers backend call and shows suggestions.
Outfit combinations section displays at least 5 groupings.
Each suggested product card links to the Shop page.

requirements.text: Build a Virtual Try-On page with a 3D outfit visualizer. Display a static 3D avatar (using Three.js / React Three Fiber) that can be dressed with selected clothing items. When the user selects a product from the shop, it appears on the avatar. Show an auto-size recommendation panel based on measurements from the user's Style Profile (height, weight, chest). Display a simulated 'Returns Probability Score' (e.g. 'Low Return Risk: 94% fit confidence') based on size match.
acceptanceCriteria: 3D avatar is rendered using React Three Fiber and is interactive (rotatable).
Selecting a product updates the avatar's outfit display.
Size recommendation is shown based on saved profile measurements.
Returns Probability Score is displayed per selected outfit.

requirements.text: Build a Smart Occasion Agent page where users type a free-text occasion description (e.g. 'I have a college fest next week'). The page parses keywords from the input (occasion type, formality, season) and calls searchProducts to return 3 curated outfit suggestions, each showing a complete look: top, bottom, footwear, and accessory. Display each outfit as a 'Look Card' with all items, estimated total price in INR, and an 'Add Full Look to Cart' button.

quotes: User types: 'I have a college fest next week.'

acceptanceCriteria: Occasion input field accepts free text and submits on Enter or button click.
3 Look Cards are displayed after submission, each with 4 item types.
Total price per look is calculated and shown in INR.
'Add Full Look to Cart' adds all items in the look to the cart state.

requirements.text: Implement a persistent shopping cart accessible site-wide via a cart icon in the navigation bar. Cart state is managed client-side (React state / context). The cart drawer/panel shows: item name, image, price, quantity controls, and remove button. Display cart total in INR. Include a 'Proceed to Checkout' button (checkout can be a confirmation screen — no payment integration required).
acceptanceCriteria: Cart icon in nav shows item count badge.
Cart drawer opens on click and lists all added items.
Quantity can be increased/decreased; items can be removed.
Total price updates reactively.
Proceed to Checkout shows a confirmation/summary screen.

requirements.text: Apply a bold, futuristic dark-fashion visual theme across the entire application. Use a near-black background (#0A0A0A or similar), high-contrast accent in electric gold/amber (#F5A623 or similar), sharp sans-serif typography (e.g. Inter or Space Grotesk), and subtle glassmorphism card styles. Navigation should be a sticky dark navbar with the AURAWEAR wordmark logo. The overall aesthetic should feel premium, tech-forward, and aspirational — targeting fashion-conscious Gen Z users.

quotes: Your Style. Your Data. Your AI.

acceptanceCriteria: All pages use the dark background and gold/amber accent consistently.
Typography is sharp, modern, and legible across all screen sizes.
Navigation bar is sticky, contains AURAWEAR logo/wordmark, and links to all main pages.
Cards use glassmorphism styling (frosted glass effect with border glow).
Design feels cohesive and premium across all pages.

requirements.text: Seed the backend with at least 20 realistic clothing products for the AURAWEAR catalog spanning categories: Tops, Bottoms, Outerwear, Accessories, Footwear. Include diverse tags (streetwear, minimal, luxury, casual, formal), price range ₹500–₹8000, multiple sizes, and varied colors. Mark 6–8 products as isTrending=true.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 20 products are available in the catalog on first load.
Products span all five categories.
Price range covers ₹500–₹8000.
At least 6 products have isTrending=true.
Tags include streetwear, minimal, luxury, casual, formal variants.

constraints: No real AI/LLM integrations — all AI agent behaviors must be simulated using rule-based logic, keyword parsing, and backend data queries.
No real payment processing — checkout flow ends at a confirmation screen.
No external API integrations (weather, Instagram, social media scraping) — simulate with static/seeded data.
No real AR/camera access — Virtual Try-On uses a static 3D avatar rendered with React Three Fiber.
All prices must be displayed in Indian Rupees (₹).
All backend logic must remain in a single Motoko actor.
nonGoals: Real-time AI/ML model inference or LLM integration.
Instagram or LinkedIn social media API integration or posting.
User authentication via Internet Identity (profiles use anonymous principal for MVP).
On-demand manufacturing or inventory management backend.
B2B SaaS dashboard for other brands.
Pitch deck, revenue projection documents, or LinkedIn post generation.
